design: Strictly sequential (Section 27's recommended order, not a joint search): main.cpp resolves --kv adaptive into a concrete Q8/Q5 mode FIRST (existing Phase 11A resolve_gpu_config()/resolve_cpu_adaptive_kv() logic, completely unmodified by this phase), then resolve_kv_placement() is called AFTERWARD with effective_kv_mode (the resolved concrete mode, passed by the caller as effective_o.kv_mode -- never MEMBRANE_KV_STORE_ADAPTIVE itself) to compute the per-layer KV byte cost the residency planner needs. Adaptive's own precision semantics are untouched -- this phase never changes which mode adaptive picks.
joint_planning_research_note: Section 28 raises whether a joint precision+placement search could beat sequential (e.g. Q8-split preferred over Q5-all-GPU purely for quality, since Phase 12G found no measured throughput penalty from CPU-resident KV in the tested regime). Phase 12H deliberately does NOT implement this -- no evidence was gathered in this phase to justify overriding adaptive's existing, already-validated Q8-vs-Q5 policy. Documented here as a legitimate future joint-planning opportunity, not built.
